documents.content:
Threat model — the public API in shop
3 entry points, 4 threats, 2 open

## Assets
- customer orders and addresses — the orders table (shop/db.py)
- the payment key — PAYMENT_KEY read at shop/config.py:2 from the environment
- the ability to run code on the host — anything that reaches `subprocess` (shop/export.py:4)

## Entry points
1. POST /orders — shop/routes/public.py:4 — anyone
2. GET /orders/{id} — shop/routes/public.py:8 — a signed-in user
3. POST /admin/export — shop/routes/admin.py:1 — an admin

## Threats
1. 2 — a signed-in user — reads another customer's order by guessing the id — I (disclosure)
2. 1 — anyone — sends 10,000 orders a minute and fills the database — D (denial)
3. 3 — an admin — the export's format field reaches `subprocess` as part of a shell command — E (elevation)
4. 1 — anyone — posts an order with a negative quantity for a refund — T (tampering)

## Mitigations
1. none — the handler loads by id without checking the owner (shop/routes/public.py:10)
2. a rate limit of 60/minute per address — shop/middleware.py:1
3. none — the format string is joined into the command (shop/export.py:4)
4. quantity must be ≥ 1 — shop/models.py:2

## Open
- 3 — code on the host behind an admin login; fix: pass the format as an argument list, never a string.
- 1 — every customer's orders behind any login; fix: filter by the signed-in user at shop/routes/public.py:10.
- not read: shop/db.py.
